1. A retract actuator assembly for a landing gear assembly of an aircraft, comprising:a retract actuator, comprising:
an actuator housing defining a longitudinal axis extending through a distal end and a proximal end, the actuator housing comprising a cylinder bore along the longitudinal axis; and
a piston disposed within the cylinder bore and configured to move within the cylinder bore along the longitudinal axis, the cylinder bore defining a piston stroke within the actuator housing that defines limits for movement of the piston, the piston stroke comprising an extended piston position relating to the distal end of the actuator housing and a retracted piston position relating to the proximal end of the actuator housing; and
a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the actuator housing in relation to the extended piston position within the cylinder bore and the retracted piston position within the cylinder bore, the kneel stop assembly configured to selectively establish a kneel stop position within the cylinder bore to reduce the piston stroke by inhibiting movement of the piston to the retracted piston position.
2. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1, further comprising:a shock absorber secured to the proximal end of the actuator housing such that the shock absorber and retract actuator are aligned along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing to form an inline shock absorber actuator, the shock absorber configured to pivotally attach to a trailing arm of the landing gear assembly.
3. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the piston defines a rod chamber in the cylinder bore relating to the distal end of the actuator housing and a piston chamber in the cylinder bore relating to the proximal end of the actuator housing, the retract actuator further comprising:
a piston rod disposed within the rod chamber and comprising a first end attached to the piston and a second end extending through a sealed aperture at the distal end of the actuator housing.
4. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 3 wherein the second end of the piston rod is configured to pivotally attach to a fixed point on the aircraft, the retract actuator assembly further comprising:a shock absorber secured to the proximal end of the actuator housing such that the shock absorber and retract actuator are aligned along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing to form an inline shock absorber actuator, the shock absorber configured to pivotally attach to a trailing arm of the landing gear assembly.
5. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 4 wherein a mechanical linkage for the landing gear assembly comprises a trailing arm of the landing gear assembly and the inline shock absorber actuator.
6. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 3 wherein the proximal end of the actuator housing is configured to pivotally attach to a fixed point on the aircraft, the retract actuator assembly further comprising:a shock absorber mechanically linked to the second end of the piston rod, the shock absorber configured to pivotally attach to a trailing arm of the landing gear assembly.
7. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 6 wherein a mechanical linkage for the landing gear assembly comprises a trailing arm of the landing gear assembly, the shock absorber, the retract actuator and a linking member between the retract actuator and the shock absorber.
8. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 3, the retract actuator further comprising:a rod hydraulic port disposed proximate the distal end of the actuator housing to provide fluidic access to the rod chamber; and
a piston hydraulic port disposed proximate the proximal end of the actuator housing to provide fluidic access to the piston chamber.
9. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the extended piston position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a fully extended condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a landing sequence of the aircraft.
10. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the retracted piston position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a fully retracted condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a takeoff sequence of the aircraft.
11. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the kneel stop position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a kneeling condition of the landing gear assembly during ground operations of the aircraft.
12. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to permit the piston to move from the kneel stop position to the extended piston position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore.
13. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1 wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to selectively remove the kneel stop position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore to permit movement of the piston to the retracted piston position of the piston stroke.
14. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 1, the kneel stop assembly comprising:a kneel stop housing secured to the exterior surface of the actuator housing of the retract actuator in relation to the extended piston position within the cylinder bore of the retract actuator and the retracted piston position within the cylinder bore, the kneel stop housing comprising a kneel stop distal end closer to the distal end of the actuator housing and a kneel stop proximal end closer to the proximal end of the actuator housing, the kneel
stop housing defining a cavity between an interior surface of the kneel stop housing and the exterior surface of the actuator housing;a kneel stop insert port disposed on the kneel stop housing to provide fluidic access to a kneel stop insert chamber formed within the cavity; and
a kneel stop withdraw port disposed on the kneel stop housing to provide fluidic access to a kneel stop withdraw chamber formed within the cavity.
15. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 14 wherein the kneel stop insert port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and the kneel stop assembly is configured to establish the kneel stop position in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid at the kneel stop insert port.
16. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 15 wherein the pressurized fluid comprises at least one of a pressurized hydraulic fluid, a pressurized oil, a compressed gas and a compressed air.
17. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 15 wherein the kneel stop insert port is configured to permit the pressurized fluid to exit the kneel stop assembly after the pressurized fluid is no longer applied by the pressurized fluid source and the kneel stop assembly is configured such that exiting of the pressurized fluid via the kneel stop insert port does not impact a current state of the kneel stop position.
18. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 14 wherein the kneel stop withdraw port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and the kneel stop assembly is configured to remove the kneel stop position in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid at the kneel stop withdraw port.
19. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 18 wherein the kneel stop withdraw port is configured to permit the pressurized fluid to exit the kneel stop assembly and the kneel
stop assembly is configured such that exiting of the pressurized fluid via the kneel withdraw port does not impact a current state of the kneel stop position.
20. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 14, the kneel stop assembly further comprising:at least one kneel stop segment disposed within the cavity of the kneel stop housing at a predetermined point along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing, the predetermined point associated with the kneel stop position, the actuator housing comprising at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the actuator housing to the cylinder bore, the at least one kneel stop aperture configured to receive at least a portion of the at least one kneel stop segment, the at least one kneel stop segment configured for selective insertion into the at least one kneel stop aperture and configured for selective removal from the at least one kneel stop aperture.
21. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 20, wherein the at least one kneel stop segment comprises at least two kneel stop segments radially dispersed around the actuator housing at the predetermined point, wherein the at least one kneel stop aperture comprises at least two kneel stop apertures radially dispersed around the actuator housing in relation to the at least two kneel stop segments.
22. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 20, the at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly comprising at least one of two kneel stop segments, three kneel stop segments, four kneel stop segments, five kneel stop segments and six kneel stop segments, correspondingly, the at least one kneel stop aperture of the retract actuator comprising at least one of two kneel stop apertures, three kneel stop apertures, four kneel stop apertures, five kneel stop apertures and six kneel stop apertures.
23. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 20 wherein the kneel stop insert port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and the kneel stop assembly is configured to insert the at least one kneel stop segment into the at least one
kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing to establish the kneel stop position in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid at the kneel stop insert port.
24. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 20 wherein the kneel stop withdraw port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and the kneel stop assembly is configured to withdraw the at least one kneel stop segment from the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing to remove the kneel stop position in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid at the kneel stop withdraw port.
25. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 20, the kneel stop assembly further comprising:an upper biasing member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and proximate the kneel stop distal end of the kneel stop housing;
an upper slider member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and between the upper biasing member and the at least one kneel stop segment, the upper slider member comprising a first portion of an upper slider exterior surface facing the interior surface of the kneel stop housing, the first portion of the upper slider exterior surface and an opposing portion of the interior surface for the kneel stop housing are configured to form the kneel stop insert chamber, the upper biasing member configured to bias the upper slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment;
a lower biasing member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and proximate the kneel stop proximal end of the kneel stop housing; and
a lower slider member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and between the at least one kneel stop segment and the lower biasing member, the lower slider member comprising a first portion of a lower slider exterior surface facing the interior surface of the kneel stop housing, the first portion of the lower slider exterior surface and an opposing portion of the interior surface for the kneel stop housing are configured to form the kneel stop withdraw chamber, the lower biasing member configured to bias the lower slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment.
26. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 25, the upper slider member further comprising:a second portion of the upper slider exterior surface in opposing geometric relation with an upper surface of the at least one kneel stop segment; and
a third portion of the upper slider exterior surface adjacent to a corresponding portion of the exterior surface of the actuator housing,
wherein the second portion of the upper slider exterior surface rises at a predetermined angle from the third portion of the upper slider exterior surface to the first portion of the upper slider exterior surface to facilitate withdrawing the at least one kneel stop segment from the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing,
wherein the first portion of the upper slider exterior surface and the third portion of the upper slider exterior surface are configured to slide between the at least one kneel stop segment and the exterior surface of the actuator housing in response to application of pressure at the kneel stop withdraw port to block the at least one kneel stop segment from being inserted into the at least one kneel stop aperture.
27. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 25, the lower slider member further comprising:a second portion of the lower slider exterior surface in opposing geometric relation with a lower surface of the at least one kneel stop segment; and
a third portion of the lower slider exterior surface adjacent to a corresponding portion of the interior surface of the kneel stop housing,
wherein the second portion of the lower slider exterior surface falls at a predetermined angle from the first portion of the lower slider exterior surface to the third portion of the lower slider exterior surface to facilitate inserting the at least one kneel stop segment into the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing,
wherein the first portion of the lower slider exterior surface and the third portion of the lower slider exterior surface are configured to slide between the at least one kneel stop segment and the interior surface of the kneel stop housing in response to application of pressure at the kneel stop insert port to block the at least one kneel stop segment from being withdrawn from the at least one kneel stop aperture.
28. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 25 wherein the kneel stop insert port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and to provide the pressurized fluid to the kneel stop insert chamber, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to move the upper slider member toward the upper biasing member and away from the at least one kneel stop segment in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid by the kneel stop insert chamber, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to move the lower slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment in response to the upper slider member moving away from the at least one kneel stop segment and the lower biasing member biasing the lower slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to insert the at least one kneel stop segment into the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing in response to the lower slider member moving toward the at least one kneel stop segment and pushing the at least one kneel stop segment into the at least one kneel stop aperture to establish the kneel stop position within the cylinder bore of the retract actuator.
29. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 28 wherein, after the at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly is inserted into the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing, the lower biasing member, the lower slider member and the at least one kneel stop segment are configured such that the lower slider member is moved into a locking position that maintains the at least one kneel stop segment inserted into the at least one kneel stop aperture with or without pressure applied to the kneel stop insert port until pressure is applied to the kneel stop withdraw port.
30. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 25 wherein the kneel stop withdraw port is configured to receive a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source and to provide the pressurized fluid to the kneel stop withdraw chamber, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to move the lower slider member toward the lower biasing member and away from the at least one kneel stop segment in response to receipt of the pressurized fluid by the kneel stop withdraw chamber, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to move
the upper slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment in response to the lower slider member moving away from the at least one kneel stop segment and the upper biasing member biasing the upper slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment, wherein the kneel stop assembly is configured to withdraw the at least one kneel stop segment from the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing in response to the upper slider member moving toward the at least one kneel stop segment and pushing the at least one kneel stop segment away from the at least one kneel stop aperture to remove the kneel stop position from the cylinder bore of the retract actuator.
31. The retract actuator assembly of Claim 30 wherein, after the at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly is withdrawn from the at least one kneel stop aperture of the actuator housing, the upper biasing member, the upper slider member and the at least one kneel stop segment are configured such that the upper slider member is moved into a locking position that maintains the at least one kneel stop segment withdrawn from the at least one kneel stop aperture with or without pressure applied to the kneel stop withdraw port until pressure is applied to the kneel stop insert port.
32. A landing gear assembly for an aircraft, comprising:a retract actuator, comprising:
an actuator housing defining a longitudinal axis extending through a distal end and a proximal end, the actuator housing comprising a cylinder bore along the longitudinal axis; and
a piston disposed within the cylinder bore and configured to move within the cylinder bore along the longitudinal axis, the cylinder bore defining a piston stroke within the actuator housing that defines limits for movement of the piston, the piston stroke comprising an extended piston position relating to the distal end of the actuator housing and a retracted piston position relating to the proximal end of the actuator housing;
a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the actuator housing in relation to the extended piston position within the cylinder bore and the retracted piston
position within the cylinder bore, the kneel stop assembly configured to selectively establish a kneel stop position within the cylinder bore to reduce the piston stroke by inhibiting movement of the piston to the retracted piston position;a trailing arm comprising an arm proximal end and an arm distal end, the arm distal end configured to pivotally attach to a fixed point on the aircraft, the arm proximal end configured to attach to a surface contact assembly; and
a shock absorber mechanically linked to the retract actuator and configured to pivotally attach to the trailing arm.
33. The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the shock absorber is secured to the proximal end of the actuator housing such that the shock absorber and retract actuator are aligned along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing to form an inline shock absorber actuator.

The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the piston defines a rod chamber in the cylinder bore relating to the distal end of the actuator housing and a piston chamber in the cylinder bore relating to the proximal end of the actuator housing, the retract actuator further comprising:a piston rod disposed within the rod chamber and comprising a first end attached to the piston and a second end extending through a sealed aperture at the distal end of the actuator housing.
35. The landing gear assembly of Claim 34 wherein the second end of the piston rod is configured to pivotally attach to a second fixed point on the aircraft and the shock absorber is secured to the proximal end of the actuator housing such that the shock absorber and retract actuator are aligned along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing to form an inline shock absorber actuator.
36. The landing gear assembly of Claim 35 wherein a mechanical linkage for the landing gear assembly comprises the trailing arm and the inline shock absorber actuator.
37. The landing gear assembly of Claim 34 wherein the second end of the piston rod in the retract actuator is mechanically linked to the shock absorber and the proximal end of the actuator housing is configured to pivotally attach to a second fixed point on the aircraft.
38. The landing gear assembly of Claim 37 wherein a mechanical linkage for the landing gear assembly comprises the trailing arm, the shock absorber, the retract actuator and a linking member between the retract actuator and the shock absorber.
39. The landing gear assembly of Claim 34, the retract actuator further comprising:a rod hydraulic port disposed proximate the distal end of the actuator housing to provide fluidic access to the rod chamber; and
a piston hydraulic port disposed proximate the proximal end of the actuator housing to provide fluidic access to the piston chamber.
40. The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the surface contact assembly comprises at least one of a wheel and a ski.
41. The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the extended piston position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a fully extended condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a landing sequence of the aircraft.
42. The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the retracted piston position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a fully retracted condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a takeoff sequence of the aircraft.
43. The landing gear assembly of Claim 32 wherein the kneel stop position of the piston stroke within the cylinder bore relates to a kneeling condition of the landing gear assembly during ground operations of the aircraft.

The landing gear assembly of Claim 32, the kneel stop assembly comprising:a kneel stop housing secured to the exterior surface of the actuator housing of the retract actuator in relation to the extended piston position within the cylinder bore of the retract actuator and the retracted piston position within the cylinder bore, the kneel stop housing comprising a kneel stop distal end closer to the distal end of the actuator housing and a kneel stop proximal end closer to the proximal end of the actuator housing, the kneel stop housing defining a cavity between an interior surface of the kneel stop housing and the exterior surface of the actuator housing;
a kneel stop insert port disposed on the kneel stop housing to provide fluidic access to a kneel stop insert chamber formed within the cavity; and

The landing gear assembly of Claim 46, the kneel stop assembly further comprising:at least one kneel stop segment disposed within the cavity of the kneel stop housing at a predetermined point along the longitudinal axis of the actuator housing, the predetermined point associated with the kneel stop position, the actuator housing comprising at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the actuator housing to the cylinder bore, the at least one kneel stop aperture configured to receive at least a portion of the at least one kneel stop segment, the at least one kneel stop segment configured for selective insertion into the at least one kneel stop aperture and configured for selective removal from the at least one kneel stop aperture.

The landing gear assembly of Claim 47, wherein the at least one kneel stop segment comprises at least two kneel stop segments radially dispersed around the actuator housing at the predetermined point, wherein the at least one kneel stop aperture comprises at least two kneel stop apertures radially dispersed around the actuator housing in relation to the at least two kneel stop segments.
49. The landing gear assembly of Claim 47, the kneel stop assembly further comprising:an upper biasing member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and proximate the kneel stop distal end of the kneel stop housing;
an upper slider member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and between the upper biasing member and the at least one kneel stop segment, the upper slider member comprising a first portion of an upper slider exterior surface facing the interior surface of the kneel stop housing, the first portion of the upper slider exterior surface and an opposing portion of the interior surface for the kneel stop housing are configured to form the kneel stop insert chamber, the upper biasing member configured to bias the upper slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment;
a lower biasing member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and proximate the kneel stop proximal end of the kneel stop housing; and
a lower slider member disposed within the cavity between the kneel stop housing and the actuator housing and between the at least one kneel stop segment and the lower biasing member, the lower slider member comprising a first portion of a lower slider exterior surface facing the interior surface of the kneel stop housing, the first portion of the lower slider exterior surface and an opposing portion of the interior surface for the kneel stop housing are configured to form the kneel stop withdraw chamber, the lower biasing member configured to bias the lower slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment.
50. A method for kneeling a landing gear assembly of an aircraft, comprising:
performing ground operations with for aircraft in which the landing gear assembly is in a fully extended condition and a retract actuator of the landing gear assembly is in an extended piston position;
activating a kneeling feature of the landing gear assembly to establish a kneel stop position in the retract actuator that reduces a piston stroke for the retract actuator by inhibiting movement of a piston in the retract actuator beyond the kneel stop position toward a retracted piston position; and
moving the landing gear assembly from the fully extended condition to a kneeling condition by moving the retract actuator from the extended piston position to the kneel stop position.
51. The method of Claim 50 wherein the extended piston position of the piston stroke within a cylinder bore of the retract actuator relates to the fully extended condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a landing sequence of the aircraft.
52. The method of Claim 50 wherein the retracted piston position of the piston stroke within a cylinder bore of the retract actuator relates to a fully retracted condition of the landing gear assembly in conjunction with a takeoff sequence of the aircraft.
53. The method of Claim 50 wherein the kneel stop position of the piston stroke within a cylinder bore of the retract actuator relates to the kneeling condition of the landing gear assembly during ground operations of the aircraft.
54. The method of Claim 50, further comprising:moving the landing gear assembly from the kneeling condition to the fully extended condition by moving the retract actuator from the kneel stop position to the extended piston position while the kneeling feature of the landing gear assembly remains activated.
55. The method of Claim 50, further comprising:establishing the kneel stop position in the retract actuator in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop insert port of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator.
56. The method of Claim 55, further comprising:permitting the pressurized fluid to exit the kneel stop assembly via the kneel stop insert port after the pressurized fluid is no longer applied by the pressurized fluid source without impacting a current state of the kneel stop position.
57. The method of Claim 50, further comprising:establishing the kneel stop position in the retract actuator by inserting at least one kneel stop segment of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator into at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the exterior surface to a cylinder bore of the retract actuator in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop insert port of the kneel stop assembly.
58. The method of Claim 50, further comprising:establishing the kneel stop position in the retract actuator by:
moving an upper slider member of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator toward an upper biasing member of the kneel stop assembly and away from at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop insert chamber of the kneel stop assembly via a kneel stop insert port of the kneel stop assembly, wherein the at least one kneel stop segment is no longer locked and free to move laterally between an interior surface of the kneel stop housing and the exterior surface of the retract actuator after the upper slider member moves toward the upper biasing member;
moving a lower slider member of the kneel stop assembly toward the at least one kneel stop segment in response to the upper slider member moving away from
the at least one kneel stop segment, the at least one kneel stop segment being free to move laterally and a lower biasing member biasing the lower slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment; and
inserting the at least one kneel stop segment into at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the exterior surface to a cylinder bore of the retract actuator in response to the lower slider member moving toward the at least one kneel stop segment and opposing tapered surfaces of the lower slider member pushing the at least one kneel stop segment into the at least one kneel stop aperture to establish the kneel stop position within the cylinder bore of the retract actuator.
59. The method of Claim 58, further comprising:locking the kneel stop position in the retract actuator after the at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly is inserted into the at least one kneel stop aperture of an actuator housing; and
maintaining the at least one kneel stop segment inserted into the at least one kneel stop aperture with or without pressure applied to the kneel stop insert port until pressure is applied to a kneel stop withdraw port of the kneel stop assembly.
60. The method of Claim 50, further comprising:deactivating the kneeling feature of the landing gear assembly to remove the kneel stop position from the retract actuator to permit movement of the piston to the retracted piston position of the piston stroke;
starting a takeoff sequence for the aircraft in which the landing gear assembly is in the fully extended condition and the retract actuator of the landing gear assembly is in the extended piston position; and
completing the takeoff sequence and performing flight operations for the aircraft in which the landing gear assembly is in a fully retracted condition and the retract actuator is in the retracted piston position.
61. The method of Claim 60, further comprising:
removing the kneel stop position from the retract actuator in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop withdraw port of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator.
62. The method of Claim 61, further comprising:permitting the pressurized fluid to exit the kneel stop assembly via the kneel stop withdraw port after the pressurized fluid is no longer applied by the pressurized fluid source without impacting a current state of the kneel stop position.
63. The method of Claim 60, further comprising:removing the kneel stop position from the retract actuator by withdrawing at least one kneel stop segment of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator from at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the exterior surface to a cylinder bore of the retract actuator in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop withdraw port of the kneel stop assembly.
64. The method of Claim 60, further comprising:removing the kneel stop position from the retract actuator by:
moving a lower slider member of a kneel stop assembly secured to an exterior surface of the retract actuator toward a lower biasing member of the kneel stop assembly and away from at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly in response to receiving a pressurized fluid from a pressurized fluid source at a kneel stop withdraw chamber of the kneel stop assembly via a kneel stop withdraw port of the kneel stop assembly, wherein the at least one kneel stop segment is no longer locked and free to move laterally between an interior surface of the kneel stop housing and the exterior surface of the retract actuator after the lower slider member moves toward the lower biasing member;
moving an upper slider member of the kneel stop assembly toward the at least one kneel stop segment in response to the lower slider member moving away from the at least one kneel stop segment, the at least one kneel stop segment being
free to move laterally and an upper biasing member biasing the upper slider member toward the at least one kneel stop segment; and
withdrawing the at least one kneel stop segment from at least one kneel stop aperture extending through the exterior surface to a cylinder bore of the retract actuator in response to the upper slider member moving toward the at least one kneel stop segment and opposing tapered surfaces of the upper slider member pushing the at least one kneel stop segment away from the at least one kneel stop aperture to remove the kneel stop position from the cylinder bore of the retract actuator.
65. The method of Claim 64, further comprising:locking out activation of the kneel stop position in the retract actuator after the at least one kneel stop segment of the kneel stop assembly is withdrawn from the at least one kneel stop aperture of an actuator housing; and
maintaining the at least one kneel stop segment withdrawn from the at least one kneel stop aperture with or without pressure applied to the kneel stop withdraw port until pressure is applied to a kneel stop insert port of the kneel stop assembly.
